utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I was informed that there were some procedural matters to be raised prior to the Prosecution calling its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President there are two issues. The first issue is the actual exhibit list of the Prosecution that has gone through revisions as late as last night. The approximate numbers of that are 148, possibly 149 documents. Ninety-three of those documents are not on the 65 ter list nor has there been any motion to add them to that list. So, certainly, given that caveat we would object to the admission of any one of those documents. I don't know in you want to take them one at a time. That is the first issue. I have before you the Mr. President, the four binders that represent virtually all of the documents that are here. I will say that we got the first exhibit list from the Prosecution on the 9th of February, missing 30 outstanding translations. The next list came the 12th February with 29 outstanding translations. Third list was the 16th, with 16 outstanding translations, and I do believe we got a few more last night. In any event, Judge, the vast majority of these exhibit, some, of course, have been used before, but a vast majority of them -- there been no motion to put them on the 65 ter lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo, this calls for an explanation, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. With respect to documents that are not on the 65 ter list, our intention was to address those at the time that we were either putting them to the witness or moving these across the bar table. Many of these, in fact, the vast majority are attachments to the four documents drafted by the witness. And they are appended to his reports by him. They are cited in his reports, and we believe that, for that reason, also the relevance and probative value of those they should be heard, but I was attempting to address that at the time that they're going to be offered. In terms of when we got them, when we disclosed them, there are a few other documents which we received quite late. There's, I believe, only two or three of those that came since the motion was filed. I think with respect to the rest of the documentation there are many of the artillery bar table documents, and I believe the court's specific direction of those was to bring them in through a particular witness; and at the time that the document was brought up we would have the discussion when they were had, when disclosed, and whether or not they should make it on to the 65 ter list. So my intention was to address those document by document for the ones that I put to the witness, and for the bar table ones to simply offer the fact that they have been attached by the witness to his statements. And with respect to the outstanding translations, Your Honour, I believe there are only three left that we have not had translated up till now. The iterations of the exhibit list have included as Mr. Kehoe has pointed out a number of translations as we have continued to get them in since the time they were submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I have a brief response Mr. President. The first issue, of course, is that just two days ago, I believe, maybe three, but I think it was two days ago, the Prosecution filed a motion before the Chamber to add a document to the 65 ter list. The question, the rhetorical question, is how come no such motion was made with respect to the rest of these documents, the rest of the 93. When the Prosecution filed its motion to add Mr. Rajcic to the witness list in 16 December 2008, the Prosecution was in possession of all of these documents absent two. And the two that were not in their -- absent three, excuse me, the two not in their possession were 65 ter 7144, and 65 ter 7145. The last document that was -- the motion was filed on two days ago, the representation of the Prosecution was that it was not in their possession. The rest of those documents were, in fact, in the possession of the Prosecutor. Now, when Your Honours -- the Chamber in its decision of 6th February, 2008, granted the request of the Prosecutor, A, to allow Mr. Rajcic to testify; and B allowed the Prosecution to add four documents to its 65 ter list. Your Honours commented in two different occasions on paragraph 21 of that document, that -- the documents had "only recently become available to the Prosecution." But, two, documents are limited in number and of are relative brevity. That's in paragraph 22. Now, clearly, Your Honours, when Your Honours were allowing the Prosecution to add these additional four exhibits, certainly Your Honours were not contemplating the array of documents that were not in part of the -- not part of the motion, nor have been put on the exhibit list. The reality of the situation is that as we move through here, we simply don't know what the Prosecution is intending to do. Let us put aside the fact that they were supposed to get an exhibit list 14 days prior to this witness testifying, but that didn't happen either. Now, this statement by counsel with regard to the bar table, Your Honour was very specific about what Your Honour wanted on that score, and Your Honours' opinion -- as an opinion and commentary, frankly, Judge, it's on 16 December 2008 at page 13789 and 90. Quite clearly, Your Honours did not want artillery documents put over the bar table. You wanted -- Your Honours specifically requested that the list of artillery documents be circumscribed, limited in number, and presented to a witness so Your Honours could get full information and be able to digest the documentation before it. Notwithstanding that, the Prosecution has attempted, once again, put these matters over the bar table. The reality of the situation is, Judge, that the Prosecution could have made some attempt to address this as early as last December, and they chose not to. The rule presumes prejudice to the Defence, and there is prejudice. We simply can't defend this case on the fly while we are trying to figure out what the Prosecution is attempting to do. I put before Your Honour the binders because I wanted Your Honours to take a look at what we have to deal with and scramble through over the past several days as this rolling disclosure on the part of the Prosecution comes across our transom literally on a daily basis. The bottom line of this, Judge, is that the Prosecution has grossly violated the rules, has made no attempt to abide by your Your Honours' instructions that have been previously given, and at this stage of the proceedings, the Prosecution has severely prejudiced the Defence in its preparation of this case in the methodology they close to employ. It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I want to address two point, Your Honour. First, with respect to the artillery documents, I didn't indicate at any time that we were going to be offering the artillery documents across the bar table. I don't know where that has come from. With respect to the number of documents, the Court pointed out there were 93 artillery documents in the first motion. We can see from my exhibit list now I've cut that number down to 14. Those of which I intend to show to the witness will be offered. Those which I do not show to the witness will not be offered. The size of the exhibit list, Your Honour, is merely a reflection of the fact that I don't know what the witness is going to say, in response to any of my questions, and I needed to give the Defence obviously notice of what I would show him, depending on what answers he gives me. So it is by no means and indication I will be offering every single document on this list to the Court in evidence. The second matter I would like to address is the claim of prejudice. I believe it ignores the reality of the situation, Your Honour, that this witness, not only is a Defence witness, but, in fact, worked on the Defence team. The Defence had notice at least as late as the filing of our motion, which documents were appended to Mr. Rajcic's statements since he listings them in his reports. I don't believe the Defence has been prejudiced in terms of knowing what documents the witness himself was relying on in drafting those reports. I don't believe it's accurate that they were unaware that we may seek to use what the witness indicates was the basis for the statements he made in those reports which are the attachments; and I don't believe it's reflective of reality that they were unprepared to deal with the evidence of this witness. In fact, the Gotovina Defence is the only party in this courtroom to my knowledge that knows what the witness is going to say in response to any questions. So I don't think the Court should be ignoring the fact that in this case, in these particular circumstances it is the Prosecution that is at an informational disadvantage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just -- and I don't mean to turn this into a debating society. If we go to the most recent exhibit list that has been provided by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And we can turn -- put it on Sanction, if we can and maybe I'm misreading this, but I don't think so. If we could put this on Sanction with the assistance of the court usher. Quite clearly there is a designation in there by the Prosecution that we're talking about HV artillery bar table documents. That's what I was referring to. I didn't imagine this when I was talking about their approach for putting bar table documents. I mean the bottom line for this violation of the rules is that the burden is on the Prosecution to justify their conduct in this regard. This is it not an exercise where the Defence has to show how or why they were not prejudiced. The presumption from the rule is that we were prejudiced, and there has simply been no reason offered by the Prosecution as to why they didn't do what they were supposed to do as early as -- well, as early as last December when they made the motion to the Chamber to add the four document to the list as well as Mr. Rajcic. Now with regard to the commentary of Mr. Rajcic being a part of the Defence team, the person that can speak to that most clearly for the Chamber is Mr. Misetic, so I would like to turn the floor over to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm surprised to hear that comment. Mr. Rajcic, first, the representation is that he a Defence witness. He would have been a Defence witness had the Prosecution not called him. He is a Prosecution witness and that needs to be made clear right now. We are in the Prosecution's case in chief and that needs to be again spelled out. You call the witness, he is yours. The second issue is with respect to him being a member of the Defence. He was not a member of the Defence. He was working with the Defence in the anticipation that he would eventually be a Defence witness in the case. If he were a member of the Defence then we would have a Rule 70 (A) issue here, which is whether he can be called by the Prosecution at all because Rule 70 (A), of course, talks about members of the Defence team if he -- if it were as they say, then communications with the Defence, et cetera, would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Communications with the Defence but, of course, I do not understand his testimony to be focussed primarily on his communications with members of the Defence team, but rather than his knowledge of what happened in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would have disagree you, Mr. President. That should be the focus of this. The pretext under which though he was added to the witness list was knowledge of documents in a reconstruction that he did for the Croatian government. There are references in his police interview that he was working with the Defence. Some of the information he may have gotten --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not discuss that in detail. But I got that impression from --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just one example, Mr. President, you recall that last Friday we had a debate about whether Mr. Rajcic gave documents to us or didn't give documents, whether they were returned to him if, in fact, it turns out the Prosecution now contends that he was a member of the Defence at that time then Rule 70 (A) would apply to that entire discussion, which is my point. I'm saying he was never a member of the Defence, and that's why we never raised it. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's leave it to that at this moment. Mr. Kehoe, I did not hear any response in relation to the problems Mr. Russo raised in relation to not knowing what the witness will testify, what his answers will be in question A, B, or C and that, therefore, the list is longer than one would expect, if -- if the witness would have cooperated in preparing for his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There are two issues there, Judge, that per se, the objection about the length of the list I can understand, or the statement about the length of the list, I certainly can understand, allowing for a full array of documents. My objection precedes that. Why was this list not brought to the Chamber's attention when the asked to, A, add Mr. Rajcic to the list and also to amend the 65 ter list. That would have been brought very early on, the list of documents that the Prosecution thought they would have to deal with. Now I emphasise again that absent three documents, all of those documents were in the possession of the Prosecution. And that simply no reason, the length, no reason why the Prosecution could not have brought this to the Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What you're do something you're reiterating your original argument, your not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I was just attempting. No I mean if -- if -- if you're saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... but, Mr. Russo, I would like to hear from you. Mr. Kehoe says what, no bar table, no determination of what will be bar tabled, what will not be bar tabled. I see it on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was probably simply a miscommunication. I was just identifying those documents as the ones which had been offered across the bar table -- as a bar table submission, simply that portion of the exhibit list comes from what had been offered as bar table documents. I indicated in an e-mail to the Defence when I first sent over the first exhibit list what would be offered across the bar table, and those were the attachments to Mr. Rajcic's four documents. So I thought I made that clear. But if not, it is my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're talking about the four documents you are talking mainly about the items in bold on the list. That's the second 7055, and then a bit later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. All of the documents in bold are the four which I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And they were all on the 65 ter list. You will forgive me for not having the whole list in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Those four documents were admitted to the 65 ter list pursuant to the Court' decision on our motion to add Mr. Rajcic and his four documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you say that all the other documents are mainly annexes to those reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Several of those annexes you will notice have actually already been admitted as exhibits. Some of them are on the 65 ter list. Many of them are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But still attached to reports that are on the 65 ter list. Are they --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- really attached to it or only a reference made to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well there's -- technically both. They came to us as actual attachments to the documents but also you will notice when I bring up the documents that they are listed at the end of each document; there is a list of attachments and each of those attachments is referenced in a particular portion of the reports where the witness relies on that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And were disclosed as attachments to those reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe these were all disclosed when the Court made the reports inter partes, so they were disclosed in bulk in terms of what we received through the 54 bis proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... talking past each other, but the documents that I just put on the screen that are the bar table documents are not attachments. Attachments to Mr. Rajcic report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Let's one by one. First of all, would you agree with Mr. Russo on the documents which do not appear now as bar table documents. That is on my list, but I don't know whether there is any newer list. I've got a list without a date, as a matter of fact. But where the first one, two, three, four, five, almost six full pages, give -- we start with an Official Note. Then we have 7055, Rajcic Analysis of Artillery Actions, and then it starts with annexes, annexes, annexes, up to Annex 25. Then 7064, Rajcic Analysis of Artillery use at the 1st Corps Level. And then we have attachments, attachments, starting with 6 A -- then 9 A. The next one, 7067, Rajcic, is Storm Reconstruction Analysis of Artillery, and then a list of attachments; and then attachments one, two, three, four, et cetera, et cetera, going up to eight ... up to attachment 35. Then we have 7102, list of attachments for 4 Guards Brigade portion of the reconstruction, and that starts with attachment 2; and then a long list of attachments up to where we come to the HV artillery bar table documents. I would first like to know whether you have any comments on what Mr. Russo said in relation to these attachments. So we stop at 4506.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My comment is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... just whether what he says is correct or incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That these were listed in Mr. Rajcic's reports, the answer to that is yes. They were not listed in the motion to the Chamber that they filed in December to add them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they attached to the Rajcic report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No -- not in what was filed with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they disclosed to you as attachments to those reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We had some of the attachments already, yes they were. But they were not disclosed as exhibits to be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Were they -- you gave two answers first that you had some already --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which was not my question. My question was whether disclosed to you as attachments to the reports, whether you had already some of them is another matter. Whether they were disclosed as exhibits to be used is also another matter. My question was whether they were disclosed to you as attachment of -- to the reports that were disclosed to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Not initially. When they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When were they.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That -- that -- that would have to go back to the Prosecution as to when they made these disclosures because the disclosure were not made at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what remain then to be seen is when these attachments were disclosed, even if not disclose as exhibits to be used, even you may have had some already in your possession, but we do not know when they were disclosed. Mr. Russo do you have an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. As we indicated, some of these documents were, in fact, used. You'll notice the ones which are exhibits, of course, have the exhibit numbers next to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This again is not an answer to my question because I was talking about disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And they were disclosed not all at the same time because we did have, as Mr. Kehoe indicates, we also had some of these in our possession and those had been disclosed even before we received Mr. Rajcic's reports. However, many of them -- most of them were disclosed in December of 2008, the 11th of December, which was a couple of days before we filed the motion to add the documents and to add Mr. Rajcic. As a matter of fact, the vast majority of those I see were disclosed on 11 December 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any comments on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would have to go back to the list with exactly when the disclosures took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You reserve your position on the date of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe that I can give you an accounting of that. Yes, I will disclose that position. But I still think Mr. President and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you think you're starting argument again I'm just seeking at this moment to establish facts, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would have to give you the list of when those disclosures came our way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, what the Chamber would prefer is that Defence and Prosecution would agree on what was disclosed when. Yes, that, of course -- otherwise we start hearing 12th of December, no, 15th of December. Of course, the Chamber, without getting access, full access, to all of your documentation could not even establish when it was disclosed, so if the parties would say agree on that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can send a spreadsheet to the Defence, which will indicated the dates we believe all of these were disclosed and see where the disagreement is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see whether there's any disagreements. So we have now at least established, apart from what the consequences would be, how the first six pages, how these attachments were disclosed, whether that's late or not is another matter. Now we move on to the six items -- no, we have now - let me just have a look - then we have 14 items of which three apparently are already in evidence, called artillery bar table documents. Mr. Russo, first of all, do you want to bar table them still or is that just a reference to what has been done in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It is a reference to what has been done in the past, Your Honour, it was not my intention to offer these particular documents across the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now disclosure of these documents when and how were they disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: They were all disclosed prior to the initial motion to add them across the bar table. So my position on that is the disclosure was made prior to that motion and our intention to offer those onto the 65 ter list was also obviously made in that motion. The Court gave specific direction on denying that motion without prejudice and indicated that the documents should be put to the witness individually at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Preferably, preferably. That's a word I missed in the Chamber's ruling -- the Chamber's guidance on that matter. So you say these documents to the extent not yet in evidence, it was clear that we wanted to use them as exhibits on from a certain moment and then you were more or less stopped or discouraged from dealing with them as you intended to do, and you rather deal with them in the way suggested by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move to the Official Notes of movement of use. 61 --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Those I intended to put to the witness, Your Honour. I do understand this is an objection with respect to that, but my intention was to over those individually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Individually. These are documents dating from, if I could say, Autumn 2008. When were they received, when were they disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: These were received in the -- along with the submissions from Croatia, in the 54 bis proceedings. They were disclosed on the 10th of February of 2009, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So very recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President I believe that these documents were disclosed to the Prosecution prior to the filing of the motion to add Mr. Rajcic to the witness list, if my memory serves me correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is consistent with what I indicated, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that consistent? You said -- let me just have a look. Yes, you said they were received along with the submissions from Croatia, and they were disclosed on the 10th of February. So you do agree on that, that they were --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I take counsel's word for it that it was disclosed in February. If I may just -- if I can comment on that, just briefly on these, these are notes that are taken pursuant, of course, to Your Honours' instructions to Croatia in the Rule 54 motion. This issue on these types of notes has been argued. Your Honour has made a ruling on this previously precluding this particular evidence from coming in. A ruling going to the -- to Croatia to go out and find these, these particular interviews were done pursuant to that instruction and now that being -- based on your instructions by Your Honours instruction, they are now being used by the Prosecution as clear hearsay coming in as witness statements to be put to this witness. It is clearly improper and Your Honour has so instructed previously. I believe Mr. Misetic has argued this issue previously, and he may want to add some clarity to that point, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have -- I remember that we have several decisions on Official Notes. Sometimes they were admitted into evidence, sometimes not admitted into evidence for various reasons, so if you could focus on these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The reason is simple. The ones that have been admitted in the past were admitted because they were not taken for the purposes of these proceedings. These interviews were specifically taken for purposes of these proceedings. Furthermore in the Chamber's ruling on the Rule 54 bis and the Rule 70 assertions, the Chamber made the explicit finding that the documents did not have Rule 70 protection because they were compelled and as a result once they're compelled, they can come in. If, in fact, now these statements don't enjoy Rule 70 protection because the Chamber says they were compelled to be taken, then there can be really no dispute that they were taken for the purposes of these proceedings. And if so, as such, they're inadmissible. They're not taken for any criminal proceeding in Croatia and if the Prosecution wishes to asserted that these were taken in the context of some other proceeding, then they can do that. But these particular statements were taken part of Croatia's investigation under the eight --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's an interpretation of -- certainly there was a link with these proceedings because it was the result of a 54 bis situation, so to say, whether they were taken to serve as evidence, whether that was the primary purpose or whether they were taken for the purpose of explaining what was done at the time in order to seek evidence is a matter still to be considered. The reason why I'm asking your explanation is that I find this situation, but I will discuss it with my colleagues, rather specific and not exactly the same as any of the other Official Note issues. We had the ones -- statements taken by the accused, for example, which was a very specific type. We had other, whether we taken for clearly Croatian proceedings. Here we have a -- I would say a new situation which we'll have to consider and it is appreciated that you have given your interpretation of what they were taken for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I may just add then, Judge, if there's any doubt about that then I think there is a duty to inquire of Croatia as to what their position is because this is again tied to the Rule 70 issue. So rather than us speculate on it and allowing it to come in, you would have to have some confirmation then that, in fact, these were not taken for the purposes of these proceedings, and as I indicated it is my understanding that that is, in fact, the very basis upon which the Rule 70 protection was denied. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour. I think Mr. Misetic indicated that these statements were not taken for a purposes of a criminal proceeding in Croatia. The documents themselves belie that. There is a criminal investigation currently ongoing in Croatia for purpose of which these statements were taken. Now to attempt to now link that with the Court's 54 bis order is, I believe, skipping a step. This Court did not order Croatia to conduct a criminal investigation. This Court simply ordered Croatia to broaden and intensify its investigation for certain documents. It was Croatia's decision how to proceed in doing that, and the decision they chose was to institute a criminal investigation under their domestic laws. These statements were not taken for the purposes of this proceeding but were taken, I believe Mr. Misetic's attempting arguing were taken for purposes of the 54 bis proceedings which would suggest to the Court is not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it is not the same thing then we go right back to the initial issue that has been litigated now for the past two months. They are now being brought into this proceeding precisely contrary to everything they argued for two months which was argued specifically that Rule 70 and Rule 54 apply because those statements were taken for the Rule 54 proceeding and not for this proceeding. They have argued to the contrary. And you've now allowed it to come in and cross over into this proceeding. The second point is he has now acknowledged that Croatia was doing this pursuant to the Court's order to broaden the investigation. Any suggestion, I mean, putting aside now any technical arguments. Let's look at this in reality, what really took place here, and if we honestly look at this and say what took place is that Croatia took these statements pursuant to the requests of the Office of the Prosecutor and this Trial Chamber's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, let's take in the reality, you're apparently describing two different realities, and the Chamber will have to consider which is the reality which guides us. The Chamber is sufficiently informed about that. Then we have other --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can have just one last comment on this, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If, in fact, these were in the possession of Prosecution going back to sometime prior to file motion on 16 December 2008, and while they were adding Mr. Rajcic to the witness list it begs the question if they wanted testimony from these individuals that are listed in these in these Official Notes, why their names were not added to the list as well. They chose not to but now attempt to get some back-door information in through Official Notes without calling those people before the Chamber as is clearly the proper procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, exclusively on this last observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. These note were put on this list again as I indicated with respect to many of the documents because I don't know what Mr. Rajcic intends to say. These witnesses have made indications of what happened at certain time during the operation or before, and I intend to put those to him to the extent that he is it giving us a different version of events. So I'm not saying I'm going to be offering him wholesale, but I don't know what he's going to say. I don't know where he's going to go. I'm simply trying to provide notice to the Defence that this may be one of the documents that I confront the witness with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a last series, other relevant documents. Many of them dating from the 1995 -- any issue there, as far as being on the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, as Your Honour can see, I don't know if you have the same version as I have. The italicised ones the 65 ter numbers which are italicised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one there and that's P461 then are you working from a list which is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: There are actually several.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if the list has been updated up till this night I might have missed the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: A number of those are on the 65 ter list a number are not, and a number are in fact admitted exhibits. Again these were placed on here in an attempt to provide as much notice as possible as to what I might be using with the witness depending on what he says with, Your Honour, the exception of several photographs and maps which I've lately provided to the Defence on the new exhibit lists, indicating that I might want the witness to use those maps to indicate certain locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any response --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Our position remains the same, Judge. There is no indication that these documents were not part of the Prosecution's array of documents going back months and months, and there's simply been no good cause shown by the Prosecution why it wasn't added to its motion to put it before the Chamber as adding to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided that we'll deal with the matter on a case-by-case basis. There is no way of giving a general ruling on the matter. Apart from that, the Chamber is not aware of what actually will be used and will not be used. The Chamber has heard the objections. It may be clear that the Chamber always wanted to know when it was received, when -- whether it was put on the 65 ter list, whether these were attachments to documents that were on the 65 ter list, when it was disclosed. So if there's any issue, we don't have to repeat the whole story but just pointing at received then, disclosed then, et cetera. That will then give an opportunity for the Chamber to -- to rule on the individual documents. Any other matter at this moment. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, just briefly. As Mr. Misetic informed you, I believe last week during the proceedings that we have taken a 92 ter statement from Mr. Rajcic. We have filed a motion before the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And guidance from the Chamber whether or not the Chamber wants to deal with it at the outset or wait until cross-examination and my request is simply one of information and guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, what -- first of all, we have not received a response to that motion yet, and if you would like to orally respond to it, then we'd like to hear from you. And if that response could include the timing of a decision on admission, whether we should do that right at this beginning, whether we should do it at the beginning of the cross-examination, which might cause you some problem because you could prefer to a statement being in evidence, saying you would have to do it all in re-examination when it has become evidence. I've got no idea on how would you like to proceed with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes thank you, Mr. President. My thinking on this is perhaps a bit different. First of all, I don't object to the statement itself coming into evidence. However, I do believe that it should be offered by the Defence during the cross-examination, and I do realise that I can't deal with on my direct. I didn't intend to deal with it on my direct. My position with respect to that is this is -- it's clearly a statement by the witness, offered by the Defence as part of their positive case. It does not arise from my direct examination. It does not attempt to impeach the evidence of the witness, which I will be adducing on direct examination. So in that sense, they are leading that evidence. I would asking to cross-examine the witness on that statement after the Defence puts it in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any comment on this suggestive course of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour will be guided by -- Your Honour dictates will gladly put it in on cross --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... whether you agree with the cause of action suggested by Mr. Russo or that you have any reasons to say, No, it should be dealt with immediately at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think as a practical matter I think it should be dealt with at the beginning because that is the evidence that he is bringing before the Chamber and have it before the Chamber, and it's in evidence, and we can take it from there. He can question based on that document. He can do what he -- anything he wants to do during the course of his direct examination with that document in evidence. That's, I believe, is the proper way to handled this. The document comes before the Chamber, the Chamber admits it, and counsel can use that document with his direct examination in any way he sees fit right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that's a very practical suggestion. At the same time, I think Mr. Russo is focussing more on what the position of this witness is, that the evidence this witness will bring will -- will be known to the Chamber, once we have heard his testimony in-chief. Usually, of course -- no, I would say under Rule 90 (H) there is quite a large latitude to cross-examine witnesses also on matters which have not been raised in-chief. So, therefore - and I do understand that Mr. Russo doesn't complain about that - but he says the right order is first examination-in-chief, then cross-examination, even if most of it is under Rule 90 (H) and is not in any way -- not directly related to what the witness will testify in-chief, and then I have an opportunity to re-examine the witness on matters raised under Rule 90 (H) in cross-examination. He says that's the proper procedural order. Let's just -- no, let me not -- perhaps refrain from any speculation on what could happen. Several scenarios could be imagined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I submit to the Chamber that the proper way to handle this is to bring this gentleman's statement before the Chamber at the earliest opportunity and admit it into evidence. The Prosecution then has plenty of time through this array of documents to ask questions that they want in conjunction with this statement and dovetailing it with the documents that they are trying to use in their examination. That is the most efficient and expeditious and certainly the clearest way to bring all of this information to the Chamber as efficiently as possible. As opposed to going back and forth and back and forth by getting a piece of the story based on this, and then the witness saying, You know there is my statement out there that is saying that, let's just talk about them together. Let's get it all together at the earliest opportunity to the Chamber and have the Prosecution deal with it now. The reason why we made this motion and brought it to their attention as quickly as possible is so that they could do exactly that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider how to proceed. Any other matters that the Chamber will have to decide before we proceed? Then the Chamber will take not much time but perhaps a couple of minutes to consider how to proceed. Everyone should remain standby. --- Break taken at 9.51 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has given some thorough thought to the issue Russo proceeding or Kehoe proceeding, to keep it short. The Chamber is aware of the practical advantages of having everything in evidence right from the beginning including the statement. At the same time, for the full transparency of the positions of the parties while examining the witness, whether examination-in-chief, whether cross-examination, whether re- examination, the Chamber has, after thorough deliberation, decided that we will follow the suggestion by Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kehoe, this suggested course of action also, of course, has some limitations. I mean, you don't have in evidence the statement of --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think you meant to say you were taking the position of Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes. You see how close a finish it must have been in our deliberations. Yes, I apologise for this -- well, let's say blunder, instead of mistake this time. Mr. Russo, it also puts certain limits on what can you do in examination-in-chief because the statement of the witness, the 92 ter statement is not in evidence. At the same time, of course, the Chamber will be better aware what, in this statement, will be in response to your examination-in-chief, of course. We don't know yet what you want to cover in your examination-in-chief and that may have consequences also for the later stages for the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just a couple of issues, Mr. President, certainly the documents that he tenders at this point over the bar table or through this witness are all going to come into -- as part of the examination-in-chief, and that being the case, the statement that we have before the Chamber is going to meet in large part, the evidence that I suspect is going to be presented by the Prosecution. Now, if there is yet -- Mr. Russo thinks there is something else out there, then I think that should be identified to the Chamber. Because at this point given the fact that Mr. Rajcic is, in fact, being called by the Prosecution there is no latitude in the rules to allow a cross-examination into issues when this particular statement is being presented to meet evidence that is being presented by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, of course, the Chamber does not know, and I don't know to what extent you are aware of the subject matter that will be covered in examination-in-chief. And this, of course, will have consequences later on how to proceed. I mean, if most of the cross-examination, even through 92 ter, will be evidence in support of the -- of the Defence case rather than a response to the examination-in-chief, this then may have consequences for the approach taken in re-examination. The Chamber doesn't know what Mr. Russo is going to do, and we have to wait and see; and then, of course, we may be in a position that we have to draw consequences, procedural consequences of what he did but perhaps also what he did not. The Chamber, to that extent, is now looking in a huge black hole. Mr. Russo, of course, knows what is he wants to cover in the examination-in-chief; and, of course, Mr. Russo also has read the statement, and although he, of course, can't refer to anything which is not in evidence at this moment if he had on his mind already to deal with some of the matters he knows to be in the statement as well, then, of course, the -- those portions of the statement can be considered at a later stage to be a response to what has been raised during examination-in-chief, and that might limit Mr. Russo in his re-examination, to the extent to how he could lead the witness. On the other hand, if there are matters in this statement which Mr. Russo had not on his mind to deal with in examination-in-chief, then, of course, he will consider how to approach the witness in re-examination, if, on these matters, the evidence given by the witness was primarily not as a response to the examination-in-chief but in support of the Defence case, under Rule 90 (H). So we have to carefully move forward and to constantly analyse the position of which party at what moment is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I couldn't agree with your analysis more. That is exactly the direction I was heading in, that part of the examination -- that part of the 92 ter statement that answers the examination-in-chief and to the extent that the Prosecution says it is something else and I understand it is something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is all speculation for the Chamber because if Mr. Russo is dealing with totally different matters then, of course, it might come as a surprise to some extent if view of his list. But ... Mr. Russo, are you ready to call your next witness, which is Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The Prosecution calls Witness 175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I used the name of the witness until now. I didn't refer to Witness 175 because the Chamber - I put this on the record - was informed by the victims and witness section that there would be no request for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration, that will you speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher. Could I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, you will first be examined by Mr. Russo. Mr. Russo is counsel for the Prosecution. You find him to your right. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: My name is Marko Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, I just want to take with you at the beginning here very briefly, what steps you've taken, if any, in preparation for your testimony here today. And please forgive me if I speak a bit slowly; I'm trying to keep up with the translation. Mr. Rajcic, did you review any documents relevant to this case -- or, pardon me, related to this case prior to coming to court here today?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what documents those were, if you can describe them for us?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: They were documents which relate to Operation Storm, and I was asked to do that by the government of the Republic of Croatia. They were documents that had been found in the archives, and they were made accessible to me. I was allowed to make a selection, according to the documents relevant to the period of that particular operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You indicated that these documents were made available to you by the government of Croatia. Can you give us the time-period in which you reviewed that particular set of documents?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: My first involvement was in July 2008, and then there was a pause of two and a half months, and then, once again, I worked on selecting the documents in October and November of 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And since November of 2008, have you reviewed any other documents provided to you by the government of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: This year, that is to say, towards the end of January. To the best of my recollection, the date was the 28th, I believe, and the 29th of January. I was provided with a number of reports which I looked through but nothing else. I didn't do anything else in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: These reports that you mention reviewed towards the end of January of this year, what did those reports relate to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were three reports: One, for artillery and rockets which were involved in Storm -- in Operation Storm, the artillery and rockets group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You mentioned three reports, and you've told us what one of them was. Can you recall what the other two reports were in reference to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The other reports were the classical type of report, daily reports, about the activities of the artillery and rocket group; and it stated the quantities of ammunition used per day, and I seem to remember one thing in particular, and that is that the representative of the embassy, the American embassy, the military attache in actual fact had visited the area, and had visited the artillery and rocket group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you identify for us who that military attache was, where it was that he visited, and what time-frame?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the gentleman's name was. However, I do remember having read about it and that he was in the area south of the town of Glamoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you able to give us a time-frame for when he was south of the town of Glamoc?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may of assistance, this is in one of the reports that is in the list of documents that are before the Chamber. I don't know -- if I can just help counsel in that regard. I certainly can find at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that assist you, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just trying to find out from the witness directly what he recalls, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, as you deem appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, you prepared a number of reports and analyses which we'll be going through the course of your examination. What I'd like to know is whether the documents which were provided to you by the government of Croatia, are those which you used to create those several analyses, reconstructions and reports?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I have to say that according to the methodology it was just a reconstruction rather than an analysis, and those documents exclusively helped me to make that reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm -- I just want to be clear that -- and find out from you whether the documents which you are referring to which -- upon which you made these reconstructions were only the documents provided to you by Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. Through the organ of the Ministry of Defence, or, rather, the military police. They provided me with documents, and they brought them to me to the office in which I made my selection of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Other than the government of Croatia, were you ever provided with any documents relating to Operation Storm or this case by anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber who that is?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The office of lawyers in Zagreb, Mr. Gotovina's lawyers, and they -- I had insight into some documents there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what documents those are? Are you able to identify those documents?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: There was -- they were daily reports for Artillery Group 4, and then there was the operations log-book of the Military District, as well as an operations log-book for the 4th Artillery Brigade, and we also had a working material of the 4th Artillery Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could check that page 33, line 8, check with the witness, his answer there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat your answer. You said -- you told us that you had the daily reports for Artillery Group 4. There was an operations log-book of the Military District, as well as an operations log-book for the 4th Artillery Brigade and then you said you also had... And then could you please repeat what you then said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a record of Artillery Group 3 relating to their daily activities, and that was the material they used as a work basis and the first information was recorded there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Misetic the 3 and the 4 were worrying you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clarified. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And thanks to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, were there any other documents that you were provided either by the Gotovina Defence or by anyone else in relation to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I personally had contacts with the commander of the artillery and rocket group, and -- Stipe Gotovac, and I asked him personally if he had any notes of his, if he was willing to hand them over to me, which, after some time, he did. He photocopied them and gave them to me. So those were the other documents that I used, except for the ones that I previously mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Have you spoken to anyone other than Mr. Stipe Gotovac, who, to your knowledge, may be a potential witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I don't know who could be a potential witness. It's not up to me to say. But at my own initiative in the bygone period, that is to say, since these proceedings started and the trial started, I talked to quite a number of commanders and officers who were commanders of different units at different levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to talk about these commanders that you have contacted. However, can you tell me first why you contacted them when these proceedings started?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Because I wanted to talk to them, and, on the basis of those conversations, to be able to establish what actually happened during Operation Storm and so that I gained an insight into how the artillery was deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to address a couple of issue there. Number one --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise to counsel. I think there is something lost in translation on that last answer and I'll just leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll see. Mr. Rajcic, part of your answer may be lost. I will read to you what has come to us in translation, and it reads: "Because I wanted to talk to them, and, on the basis of those conversations, to be able to establish what actually happened during Operation Storm and so that I gained an insight into how the artillery was deployed." Are we missing something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I wanted -- well, let me repeat. With the commanders I wanted to talk to them, only talk to them, to see what it was that happened with the use of the artillery and that a qualification and whether the qualification of it being used to too great a measure was correct or not, or disproportionate use of the artillery, whether that qualification stood or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And again, thanks to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, what position did you hold with the Croatian forces during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The chief of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And as the chief of artillery, were you unaware of how the artillery was deployed and used in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No. I was not unaware. I was aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That leads to my next question then. If you, in fact, were aware, why then did you need to contact commanders in order to get information about how the artillery was deployed and used?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I did not ask confirmation from the commanders or information as to how the artillery was deployed, but what it was that we did that we were being accused of disproportionate shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Two issues there. First, why did you want to know? Was this for your own personal edification, or for some other reason?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Personal reasons, because I don't think I did anything wrong anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Second issue is in speaking with these commanders, did you learn anything of which you were not already aware?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No, nothing significant, based on the recollections of those people. But finally it became quite clear that my recollections were better than theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: This is as good a time as any, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Rajcic, we'll have a break. 25 minutes. We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, we left off discussing conversations you had had with HV commanders, in respect of the artillery operations in Storm. I wonder if you could please provide us with the names of the commanders with whom you spoke.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I spoke to the commander of the 3rd Artillery Group, Mr. Mamic; the commander of the 4th Artillery Group, Mr. Milin; the commander of the 5th Artillery Group, Mr. Kardum; and the chief of artillery of the Zadar Operations Group, Mr. First; and I have already said that I went to see Mr. Stipe Gotovac at Livno.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, have you watched this trial or any of the proceedings of this trial on the Internet or on television?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: On television, I followed it to the extent that my private commitments allowed me to do so. I didn't have the chance to follow this trial on the Internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, if you can recall, which witnesses you've seen the testimony of, if any.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The names that come my mind now are Mr. Gojanovic, parts of his testimony, not the entire testimony. And Mr. Lausic's testimony, which -- which took place recently. And force the last two days, I watched Mr. Puhovski. All the other information I got by means of teletext for some witnesses, or for others through articles in the daily papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not quite certain what teletext is. Can you explain that to me?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: On television, you can browse the daily news, and you get summarised versions of the news.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up. Have you seen any of the exhibits which have been admitted in this case?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you well. Could you please repeat. Have I seen what?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Have you seen any documents which have been admitted into evidence in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Well, the documents related to the artillery. If that's what you mean. Yes, I'm familiar with them. I did see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just to be clear, when you saw documents related to the artillery, are you referring there to the documents provided to you by the government of Croatia or some other source of documents?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Other sources too. General Gotovina's Defence showed me some documents when I was giving my statement to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you able to recall what documents those were?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: They showed me one of my maps that I used in my work, as a -- as a prop. I saw a list of officers that attended a meeting on August the 1st, 1995 in Split. I saw a document relating to a staff training session that took place at the Sibenik Operations Group, under the title: Poskok. That was a document that I drafted myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, the map that you first mentioned, you indicated it was a map that you used in your work. Can you tell us about this map, what's the name of it, what use you make out of it in your work?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: It was a map that I made for myself to use in my work as an addition to the other documents that I was obliged to use. And that was the way I proceeded in all operations in which I participated in the homeland war. That map contained the ORBAT of the artillery or artillery and rocket groups, as well as the artillery units of the subordinate units that act brigades and regiments.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apology, Mr. Rajcic. I didn't understand what you said at the begin of your sentence. Let me read it back to you. It indicates: "That map contained the ORBAT of the artillery or artillery and rocket groups." Can you say that sentence again? I'm not sure what is an ORBAT is or if that was mistranslated.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I don't think that I used the word ORBAT. It must have entered the transcript by mistake. The map that showed the operations disposition of the units, that may have been the source of the error.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That map that they showed you, is that one of the maps which you attached to the analysis of the corps level artillery that you did for the government of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. I handed it over to the military police, and they decided that the map be part of the set of documents that will be handed over to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President -- I'm sorry, Mr. Registrar, if we could please have 65 ter 7058.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, I'm going to pull up a map for you and ask you if this is the map which you're referring to. Unfortunately, this is a rather large map; and, therefore, has been cut into sections, so I'm going to proceed to the portion of the map that covers the area of Knin and ask you if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could, please, Mr. Registrar move to the third page. If we could just bring that down a bit. A little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, looking at the screen, do you recognise this as the map that was shown to you by the Gotovina Defence?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a -- it was compressed when they showed to me, and this is the map that I made for the Storm operation. There is a mistake on the map too. I knew of it then, but it wasn't relevant, since this map was only a working material.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Would you mind letting us know what the mistake was.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: You can see these lines that looked like a fan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, those are the sectors of fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, the sectors of fire. The upper line, the top-most, the upper-most line, relates to the 203-millimetre Howitzers. And then there's a -- the upper line is extended till the -- to the border of this section; you can't see its end because the end of the line means the range of an artillery weapon. The 203-millimetre Howitzers have a range of 17 kilometres, and I went about it hastily and applied the range of the 130-millimetre cannon, so that the correct range to the left; that is, from the left border, is up to the fourth quadrant.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for explaining that, Mr. Rajcic. You indicated that this was a working map. Was this map actually attached to any orders issued during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would offer into evidence, 65 ter 7058 [Realtime transcript read in error, "7508"].

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm still preserving our objection concerning non-65 ter at request of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your first requested be to have it added to the 65 ter list. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And there was an attachment to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: This is it Annex 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Annex 3 working map, yes. Undated 7058.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, any specifics to be added in relation to specifically this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Nothing other than has been previously raced. On the transcript, Mr. Russo, I think it reads 7508, I think you said 7058.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, would you please assign a number for this exhibit to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this become Exhibit P2322, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, did you -- Well, let me ask first, Mr. President, can we go into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you recognise the map that is now in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is this the map entitled: Plan of artillery action, which is referenced in the document that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't have that title in this handwriting, but this is a usual -- we're talking about a usual cover page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not certain I understand what you mean by "a usual cover page." Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I mean the following. The map that we have just seen was a printed by means of a computer on a white sheet of paper and glued together. It was also a plan of artillery action. That's what it read.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when you say that, are you referring to the original of this map that we're now looking at or a different map?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I'm comparing the map that we saw earlier, before this one, I mean my working map, to this map, which was made for the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, can you explain why the map was made from the book? Was it made from another map? Was a reproduction made for the book, or was this map never in existence during Operation Storm? The content of the map, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: During Operation Storm, there was such a map in existence, and there was my handwriting on it. That map, in accordance with the rules, was always folded and scrolled to A-4 format.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what use was made during operation Storm of that map, which you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: It was used in the following manner. In addition to my working map, over which there was a transparent foil, and in the operations centre during the operation, I entered certain elements; and the original map was next to it, and I used it on -- as -- as a guideline for directing the artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When you say that you entered certain elements, does that mean information which is contained on this map that we see here in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No. Those that are made during combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: What I'm trying to discover, Mr. Rajcic, you indicated that this map, some use of it was made during Operation Storm, or at least the information on this map, there was some use of that made during Operation Storm. I'm trying to discover --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Not this one. Not this map. It wasn't the map that we see here. This is a copy of my original, the original that I used. This one here was made for the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When you say, "this is a copy of my original, the original that I used," are you saying that the original of this map that we have in front of us was used by you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: During the operation, it was in the operations centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Why was the original of this map in the operations centre?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That is normal procedure, because without the original, no control is possible, when it comes to controlling the implementation of the combat plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Does the information on this copy accurately represent the information on the original map?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, if we're speaking about the time when the original was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to ask for the assistance of the court usher because I want to focus on a particular part of this map, and that's the part of the map that covers the area of Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the map should be moved downwards and then be zoomed in. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. Focussing just a little bit more, if it's possible, on the area underneath where it says "7KK." Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, is this the portion of the map which covers Knin and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'll ask to you take particular note of the configuration of the target boxes immediately beneath the designation 7KK which I understand to mean 7th Krajina Corps; is that correct? You have to answer yes or no for the record, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 7th Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And looking at the configuration of these -- and focussing on the fire target boxes directly beneath the 7th Krajina Corps sign, the one on the far west side is going north to south. Immediately to the south-west of that, we see one that is it also going north/south. Immediately to the north of that target box, there is one slanted north-west. Immediately next to that is it a target box aligned east/west. And immediately next that is a target box aligned north/south. Do you follow me?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not, Mr. Russo. I think the second box south-east of the first one, not south-west of the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You are correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could now please have Exhibit D21. We no longer need use of the ELMO, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the completeness of the record, Mr. Russo, in order to avoid that people start guessing later what I said, I said that the second box was south-east of the first one, rather than south-west. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And, Mr. Registrar, if we could please move to page 4 of this exhibit. And we can have only one version. B/C/S is fine. I only need it for the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, looking at this map, Mr. Rajcic, first of all, let me ask you: Do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Not in this form, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Looking at the rectangular target boxes, you can see that they're in the same configuration. Would you agree with that? The same configuration as we saw on the previous map.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. But there are too many rectangles here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When you too many rectangles, are you referring to the large rectangular boxes or other rectangles?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: All the other ones round about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now looking at the legend on the bottom right-hand corner of this exhibit, it indicates targets according to M. Rajcic's plan. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that it says that, targets according to plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what I'd like to know is the plan that is referred to here, is that the map which we have previously seen?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: A map like this with all these other things, no, it's not the map. If you consider this to be a comparison with the other map, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking, Mr. Rajcic, if what is referred to in this map -- in this legend at the bottom right-hand corner, it indicates that there are -- that the black rectangular box, the larger target boxes are according to something called M. Rajcic's plan; and what I'm try to discover is whether or not the plan that is being referred to there, to your knowledge, is that the plan that we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That is in keeping with the map, but it's not the targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
