utterances.text: Thank you. And you can see, actually, also below that, in the legend, there's an indication that says "targets, according to M. Rajcic's list?" Do you see?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, just by way of foundation if the question could be asked that did this witness, in fact, prepare this. It might be helpful to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think the witness has already indicated he's never seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... from all his answers it appears that did he not. But if that is misunderstood then you'll correct that, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I don't believe it is misunderstood, Mr. President. I'm just going to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know what list is being referred to where it indicates "targets according to M. Rajcic's list"?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Targets according to M. Rajcic list, in the plan section, on an overall list we have the bases and the targets that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned that there -- that the smaller rectangles on this were not correct. Can you please explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: They are unknown to me, these rectangles, 8 and above. And also unknown to me are some of these -- well, artistic designs with the circles and the crosses. I'm not sure what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I want to be clear about which of the smaller rectangular boxes are not known to you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: 808, 839, 840, 804 and then 300 or 507, whichever it is, 306. Target 131 was never on the list of targets and now the circles within the large rectangles which designate the areas, I never did anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, just for us to understand the agenda in English, yes, now I have it, got it in English. Can we move on just a bit so that we ... that we see the upper box as well. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have Exhibit P1272.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. May I say something? At the top of this list it says overview of the fired artillery targets, Knin area, in operation Kozjak 95. This never happened. It says "fired artillery targets" in the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic. Let me another that for a moment. First of all, what do you understand it mean where it says "fired targets." What do you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: It mean that the targets were fired at.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you saying that where we see the red crosses with circles at the centre that you don't agree that those targets were fired at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could now please move to Exhibit P1272.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, looking at this target list, did you prepare this target list?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, when exactly it was that you prepared this list?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: For the staff training of the headquarters of the Split area, two or three months before Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we can now please have Exhibit P1271?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I note that we need an updated translation because we can now see the -- what is behind the shaded --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Where it says redacted, I think we had this already done in the past, isn't it? That we had identified a more legible copy of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but I believe Mr. Misetic is indicating and quite correctly that a translation of what is now visible has not been provided to the Defence, and I believe he is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which comes as a surprise because the text was already -- had become clear already at an earlier stage. So you will upload a complete translation then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at this exhibit, P1271, Mr. Rajcic, did you draft this particular list?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell us when exactly this list was drafted?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: In 1993, in the first half of the -- of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you able to tell us whether the target list we see on the screen now, if this was corrected in any way before the target list which we previously viewed was drafted?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No. You can't say it was corrected. This is a target list for a certain limited non-executed combat assignment, and the list of targets that we had on our screens before this was used for training of the staff of the Military District two years later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Were either of the target lists that we've looked at, either this one or the one we looked at previously, were either of those target lists actually used during Operation Storm by any of the artillery units?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Only certain targets were used, pursuant to my instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please identify which ones those are on this particular list.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The Slavko Rodic barracks, KV 250. Of course, I'm referring to my recollections 40 years on -- 14 years on. Then the bridge at the entrance which is KV 314 if I can see it properly. It is a little illegible. It is not quite clear what the KV number is. And KV 350 the Senjak barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just by way of clarity, the English has 310. I just make sure we're talking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that is not very clear on the original, Mr. Russo. It could well be, but we have to have a closer look at the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the bridge whether 310 or 314 is -- I will enlarge the original a bit, so that we ... Yes, if you strongly enlarge the original, then it comes closer to 310 than to 314, I would say. But it certainly is not a 4, it could be a zero.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you like me to refer the witness to the specific coordinates in order to determine whether or not this is the target he is referring to? I believe it is clear. I just want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He talked about the bridge and that's ... bridge at the entrance, that's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, apologies for the technical issues we're having. You've identified the Slavko Rodic barracks, KV 250. The bridge at the entrance, which according to our numbers is KV 310, and you have also identified, I believe, the Senjak barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. So far.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Please continue then, if you can, identifying for us the targets which were actually fired at from this list.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: KV 410 the railroad station or railway station; as for KV 510 the cross-roads, I'm not quite sure about that; KV 550, the old garage; KV 610, the apartment building complex, yes; KV 650, the Padjene warehouse, no; KV 710, the hospital, yes; KV 750, the screw and bolt factory, yes; KV 810, the western bridge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I want to be clear, but correct me if I'm wrong but I think the only one you said was not fired at was the Padjene warehouse, KV 650; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No, not only that one. I think I said no to some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Perhaps it might be easier if you simply just identify for us the ones which were not fired at.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: KV 110, the church in Knin; KV 150, Kosovo warehouse; KV 210, army barracks at the entrance; KV 450, the western warehouse; KV 510, I don't remember; KV 550, old guard house, no; KV 650, Padjene warehouse, no; and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo I don't know whether it's a translation issue but I heard when the witness read the old garage in English it became an old guard house. It is unclear to me. Could you please try to find out -- not at this very moment but whether is there a translation issue there or whether it's just --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honour, that is actually a translation issue. What we have in English as old garage, I believe, is a transliteration of the term Stara Straza. If that's incorrect, I'm sure colleagues will correct me. So I don't know that it actually refers to an old garage. Nevertheless, that is the translation that we have, and I do think you're correct that it is not -- as was indicated, I believe --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stara Straza is a toponym of the area in which military depots were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And looking at the target list for KV 550 where it indicates Stara Straza is that the location to which you are referring?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. It denotes the area where there were military warehouses or depots, logistics. Logistical resources?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I believe you indicated that did you not fire on that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That is right, I said that we didn't fire on that. And I have to mention at this point that we're talking about 130-millimetre cannons and a 122-millimetre launcher, so pieces that are listed along the side here. And in Storm, what was targeted was what I said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let me see if I can understand what you're saying. Are you indicating that some of the targets which you've just told us were not fired at, are you indicating that those may have been fired at by weapons other than a 130-millimetre or the 122-millimetre multiple-barrel rocket launcher system?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know that anybody targeted the Stara Straza target area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: How about any of the other areas that you mentioned from this list were not targeted with these weapons systems? Do you have any information that those targets were fired at by any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I do not, but I don't think they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just to be clear, if they were fired at, is there any reason that you can think of why you would not be aware of that, as chief of artillery for the Split Military District?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I would have to have known. However, if I'm not sure, then I can't say anything for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe the only target you indicated you were unsure about was the cross-roads, target KV 510. Are you unsure about whether artillery was fired at any of the other targets?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: When we were discussing the targets that were fired at, then I said, in referring to KV 510, the cross-roads, that I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. And what I'm attempting to determine is whether or not you are unsure as to whether any piece of artillery was fired at any of the other targets which you indicated were not fired at by the 130-millimetre and 122-millimetre rocket system?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, but could you repeat that question, please, once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Sure. As it stands now this is my understanding and please correct me if I'm wrong. You are unsure whether targets KV 510 was fired at with any weapon system; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly move away from the microphones. Thank you. Slightly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you move away a little bit away from your microphone, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, other than target KV 510, you indicated a list of targets that you said were definitely not fired at by the 130-millimetre gun or the 122-millimetre multiple-barrel rocket launcher system; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, as to that list of targets, which you are sure was not fired at by either the 130-millimetre gun or 122-millimetre rocket launcher systems, do you know whether those particular targets were fired at by any other type of artillery system by the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, again, as to that, would you have known if any other artillery weapons of the HV had fired at those targets?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Considering the way the control and supervision functioned at the front line, I would have had to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to digress for a bit, because we moved off of the sort of plan I wanted to follow. I wanted to discuss with you the planning of Operation Storm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, before we do that and I know it comes perhaps a little bit late. It seems that the original of the document that we just discussed there is something visible near to where a date is expected to appear, which is wiped out. I do not know it. Do we have the original? Do you have the original? Is there any way of reconstructing what the date of this document was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can tell the Court that what you see here in B/C/S is the original that we received from a request for assistance to the government of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Original means the very original not a certified copy of the original or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I don't believe we actually receive original documents pursuant to our RFA's. I believe we receive copies. This is a copy of the original, as far as we know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because from a copy it is usually impossible to reconstruct something that may be on the original but -- well, I see something appears, which is in the translation as become a line by now, which doesn't appear to me as a normal line. Although the place suggests that it's a line. But even if you underline something, often you find something above what is underlined. So I wonder whether there is any way of getting more information about -- about this document, perhaps from the original one because the date seems not to be without relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: We'll certainly investigate further, Mr. President. Let me, however, ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you indicate that you did draft this document, Mr. Rajcic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if can you recall, did you actually place a date on the document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I think the date was originally entered with a ballpoint pen. This was a template that was used at the time for making target lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when you entered the date in ballpoint pen, can you give the Court an indication of what that date was?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise indication, but I can remember the event that triggered this generation of targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what time-frame was that event?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of June, on the day of St. Anthony at Biograd. On the beach, the enemy opened artillery fire and shelled Biograd. A number of citizens were killed, including some soldiers. And one of my neighbours, a soldier, was killed on that occasion; and that is why I remember the date, because that day has been commemorated since.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Forgive my ignorance of this, but that would be 13 June of what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If the Chamber is satisfied, Your Honour, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the question remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I would like to a bit about the planning of Operation Storm. Can you tell us when planning for this operation began?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The last planning activity for Operation Storm started on July the 31st, 1995, as soon as General Gotovina and I flew back from Brioni to Rujani.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I see that you indicated that the last planning activities for Operation Storm started on July 31st, 1995. I would like to know when the first planning began.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Part of the front line from Dinara to Velebit, that was the zone of responsibility of the Split Military District, and after the separation of forces under the Zagreb Agreement, that's when the first planning activity for a possible attack operation began. That's why I'm saying that the day indicated was the last activity for planning Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And are you able to give me a day -- a date for when planning began? You indicate that part of the front line from Dinara to Velebit and the separation of forces under a Zagreb Agreement. Can you please give me a date, if you recall one, or an approximate date.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: A date for what?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: For when the planning for Operation Storm began.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: July the 31st, in the evening hours, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could please have 65 ter 7145.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at the first paragraph here, Mr. Rajcic, let me read that to you. It indicates: "Analysis of the course of combat actions, action methods and efficiency of the intelligence security in the preparation for combat, and monitoring of HD combat action, shows that it was very efficient at ZP, Military District Split, for the final Operation Oluja, Storm, especially because of the nine months continuity in preparations for the operation which is mirrored through intelligence actions during the attack operations Zima 94, that is Winter 94; SKOK, Jump; SKOK-1, Jump 1; SKOK-2, Jump 2; and Ljeto 95, Summer 95 when two 'key' OG operation groups Sjever, north, ex Livno and Sinj were active." Do you agree with this analysis, intelligence analysis?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. In this part regarding the continuous nine months beyond the Dinara, for the operations mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I would offer 65 ter 7145 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Same objection on a non-65 ter listing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a non-65 ter listing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. However, this is one of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... annexes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is it is not one of the annexes, Your Honour, but it is one that we received this year in January of 2009 pursuant to a RFA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your request is to have it added to the 65 ter list and then to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit P2324, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I also have 65 ter 2960, like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, can you see here there is a document dated 21 February 1995, and it indicates assembly and organisational points for a mobilisation plan. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the document, but I know about the mobilisation activities. I was familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is on the 65 ter list. I would move for its admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2325, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, who decided to use artillery against targets in Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Talking about military targets in Knin, Benkovac, and Gracac, I made -- I drafted the plan and submitted it to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when exactly did you submit that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, there was a limitation in the answer. Mr. Rajcic, Mr. Russo referred to the use of artillery in general terms, not against specific targets. Of course, this Chamber does not know what was targeted, but the question was put in a very general way, who decided on the use of artillery, and even you are convinced that only military targets - that may be the case - were targeted, could you please answer the question, in general terms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood the question, the Prosecutor wanted to know who planned and ordered the shelling of targets in Knin, Benkovac, and Obrovac. If that is -- is -- if I understood the question correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that the -- apparently the Gotovina Defence has difficulties in -- I -- the question was, as I read it on the transcript: "Mr. Rajcic, who decided to use artillery against targets in Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac." The answer was talking about military targets which is more limited than the question was. The question did not specify what type of targets and was just focussing on the use of artillery. So, therefore, the -- Mr. Misetic you're --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, with fairness to the witness, I think the question as phrased was who it decided to use artillery against targets in those towns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever. Whether these were civilian targets, military targets, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He can put that to him [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but that was the question. Yes, but the witness narrowed the but let's -- let's not make -- spend a lot of time on it. Mr. Rajcic, use of artillery, in general, whatever may have been targeted, was done in the way as you described? You made the plan --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when you submitted that plan to General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was on the 1st of August, after a meeting with the commanders of the units, which was held in Split. We started drafting combat documents, in accordance with General Gotovina's vision of the combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And just to be clear, are you saying that that was 1st August 1995?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Does that mean that you had not planned to fire artillery at anything, in Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac prior to 1 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: So that leaves open the possibility, if I'm not mistaken, that you had planned to fire artillery at some things in Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac prior to 1 August 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, you mean the list of targets from 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not attempting to get to a particular document or reach a particular document in time. I'm just trying to figure out when the idea to use artillery against targets in any of those towns began. And let me further clarify: Not as a matter of training exercise, but as a genuine effort to plan a potential use of artillery against things inside those towns.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I repeat, that the list of targets from 1993, which is a result of some people bathing on the beach of Biograd getting killed, and at the time, the late General Bobetko was in Zadar. As far as I remember, he gave orders to start preparations for the case anything of -- like that should be repeated, for us to retaliate against Knin, not Benkovac, Obrovac, or other towns, even though, in terms of distance, it would have been -- or, rather, it was possible to target these towns even earlier. But it never happened, not before Operation Storm, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what preparations you made, pursuant to General Bobetko's order, to plan for a retaliation against Knin? What exactly did you do?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The usual activities; namely, selecting the type of weapon, the tactical and technical processing of the target, the collection of information from the intelligence services, and from communications, electronic communications. We also had a drone which had flown over Knin. The selection of firing positions which would allow two -- to shell targets in Knin due to their range.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what was the result of those preparations, in terms of the targets that you had selected at that time, as targets for a retaliation with artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? What as a result?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: What targets in Knin had you selected at that time.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: We only produced this list, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when you say "this list," was that the last artillery target list that we looked at here in court?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. The list where the date is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I'm looking at the clock. Either now or within five minutes, I would like to start a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe now is better, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break, and we'll resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'd like to ask you a couple of more questions about your indication that you began planning the operation for the use of artillery on 1 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could please have 65 ter 5710.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just by point of clarification noted by me colleague. I think he said the final planning as opposed to the planning, if I'm not mistaken, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was your question -- you began final planning or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My question was more geared towards the date. I'm not going to quibble with counsel about the last planning activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately prior to Operation Storm. Is that what you want to refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, looking at this report on the screen, you can see it indicates -- it's dated 7th of May, 1995, and it indicates -- I believe it is from Brigadier-General Ademi to General Gotovina. It indicates: "Pursuant to your command we are ready to open fire on Knin within four hours." Let me ask you first, are you familiar with this report?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And do you know what Brigadier Ademi was prepared to fire at in Knin on the 7th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I assume. I can only assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I take that as you don't know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Judge, he said can only assume. That is his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say you can only assume, often people have reasons to assume something or not. Could you give us any fact known to you which might be relevant for making any assumptions? I'm not inviting to you make assumptions, but was there anything comes to your mind which might assist in understanding this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have to look at the time when the operation SKOK-2 was terminated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't give you any answer to that. I don't know whether there's any -- but could you indicated why that would be relevant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, because after operation SKOK-2, which came before Ljeto 95 or Summer 95, we took control of the dominant elevations on mount Dinara and at that time we had 130-millimetre cannons in the area of Veliki Cilj, which is a peak, a dominant elevation on mount Dinara, a dominant feature there; and that was the first time where from those positions we were able to fire on the settlement of Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that at a certain moment in time Knin came within the reach of your artillery from the position you had recently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... yes. Already then. Yes, already then after operation SKOK-2, we were in a position to target Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I raise yet another issue with regard to this document. It is not on the 65 ter list. It is on to the proposed list. It is not on any list that I have had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, I was going advise the Court that this is it a document that appears as a -- cited by Reynaud in his report that is Exhibit P113. This document appears at footnote 769. I did not put it on the exhibit list. I, had in fact, not come across this document. It's only come to my attention after the witness gave the answer he gave about when he started the plan for drafting artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the witness says he doesn't know anything. He sees the document for the first time. So I don't know what the probative value is of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Not sure if Your Honour wants me to answer that in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not necessarily at this very moment. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The larger question is the methodology that we seem to be employing here about not giving notice, as the Prosecution is required to do concerning this document. We've had numerous lists of exhibits and this is has not appeared at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will have it marked for identification, only at this moment and decide on admission at a later stage. Mr. Kehoe, if any new document comes up where you say it should not even be put to the witness I would not mind that you object already before Mr. Russo tenders it. Because Mr. Russo is in that respect sometimes he immediately starts tendering a document as soon as it is on the screen. Whereas in other positions, other moment, he first puts questions to the witness and if there is a -- especially here where it is neither on the 65 ter list not recently received, then I would not mind if you immediately say that, We'll then decide whether Mr. Russo can use it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, if if can I offer a procedure if a document is not on the 65 ter number list, and if it's not on the exhibit list that the Chamber can ask the Prosecution to tell the Chamber first as the exhibit comes up, as opposed to I go and scramble around for these lists to see if I somehow missed this document as I was doing my pre-trial prep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem may be that we might -- we get a document on the screen. Often 65 ter number is provisionally assigned to it. So I do not have the 65 ter list completely on my mind to immediately say, This one is not on the list, that one is on the list. If are you not able either then we would have to invite Mr. Russo to tell us right at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President I'm happy to do that. In fact, I agree I should have done that with this document. If it is not on the exhibit list which I provided I will advise counsel and Chamber prior to calling the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if it is on the exhibit list but not 65 ter list you should notifies us as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I want to be clear about that, Your Honour, if it's on the exhibit list and still not on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the complaints was that many of the documents we see here are not admitted yet to the 65 ter list so if you say if it is on the exhibit list, then if you refer to the exhibit list we received recently, then you should also make clear whether it is admitted -- whether it is on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we have sometimes two problems. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going say something but the point has been made so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Russo, please proceed, but I think we invited Mr. Registrar to assign a number for this document to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit P2326, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Rajcic, Can you tell us what Brigadier Ademi was prepared to fire at on July 5th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think, again. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we never got an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think Your Honour addressed this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is to some extent true and to some extent not true. It's true that you didn't receive an answer. But what the witness told us is that he could assume something. Then you said, So you don't know. And then I think I intervened and said, Well, sometimes there are facts known to a person on which he might base an assumption and he asked him for those facts. And he gave those facts. Although he said, I would have to check the time frame exactly to know whether there would -- could explain the situation. But to some extent you're right, when you said, So you don't know. I take it that not having looked at it, and telling us that you could assume something, that -- and also on the basis of the explanation that you then gave, may I take it that you have no specific knowledge on what Brigadier-General Ademi was specifically talking about when he said -- not that he was prepared but that he was ready to fire on Knin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For me to be able to define the text and the possibilities of targeting Knin, I would have to have information because of the area, the region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you are offering more or less a reconstruction on the basis of more information. What I'd like it know is did Mr. Ademi ever tell you what he meant by that. Was it ever explained to you by anyone what may have been the meaning of -- thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you know why -- well, let me ask you this; were you consulted at all during this time-period of May 1995 by General Gotovina or by anyone else, as to targets to be fired at with artillery in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Were you the chief of artillery for the Split Military District at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you offer any reason why you would not have been consulted, had plans been made to fire on Knin at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, that is pure speculation at this point. If plans had been made that -- first, that is the one premise, speculation and why he wasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, not this question may lead to speculation but the question is not such that the answer could only be speculative and that's the test. Could you answer the question, please. You remember the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Whether I was the chief of artillery for the Split Military District, and my answer to that was yes. Now, it says Operative Group Livno, and at that time the chief of artillery for the Operative Group of Livno was another officer, or Operations Group Livno.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us who that operations officer -- I'm sorry, can you tell us who the officer was who was the chief of artillery for Operation Group Livno at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Not with certainty, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us a name without 100 percent certainty?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: In Operation Group Livno, the chiefs of artillery changed. Mr. Bruno Milin; then there was Mr. Mamic, the two of them. I don't know when which one of the two took over duty during this particular period.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The two officers that you have named, Mr. Bruno Milin and Mr. Mamic, these were the commanders of the corps artillery groups TS-4 and TS-3 during Operation Storm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, going back to when the planning for artillery in Operation Storm began, can you explain to the Chamber a bit about how the process worked. You have already indicated that you prepared an artillery plan and submitted it to General Gotovina. Can you enlighten us as to any discussions you had with him with whether to use artillery, what the considerations were that went into the decision on whether or not to use it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: At the level of my discussions with the Commander-in-Chief and at a meeting of the 1st of August, 1995 in Split, General Gotovina expressly ordered to everyone present at that meeting -- or, rather, gave orders to everyone present, and after providing the first information and the order that preparations start for Operation Storm, a special caution, he stressed, should be taken, because of the fact that we did not have enough artillery ammunition and ammunition for tanks, that we should bear that in mind, the deficiencies there and what must be done was to conduct a special analysis into the selection and preparation of artillery pieces to be used in the most sensitive targets along enemy lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did he discuss with you any special considerations or in fact any considerations at all about the use of artillery in the populated towns of Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, or Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. If we could have add, Drvar, which is in Bosnia-Herzegovina to the list, that is in the list of towns that were in the order that I might note as being left out consistently by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, if I would say, I overlooked that, that's fine. On the other hand, of course, Mr. Kehoe is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused, Your Honour. We have been constantly facing objections about the relevance of material happening in Bosnia, at this point. I'm not saying it is irrelevant, I simply don't want to focus on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a suggestion. If you want to follow that yes or no, I leave it entirely to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, let me ask you the question again. Did you have any discussions with General Gotovina about the considerations of using artillery in the civilian-populated areas of Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you explain to us what those considerations were.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The responsibility on the part of the superior command of the Main Staff of the Croatian army, which makes it incumbent on the fact that the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska and the command posts in depth should be placed under artillery supervision.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not certain I understand what you mean by "should be placed under artillery supervision." Can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That means in the tactics applied and the deployment of the artillery, that looking at those targets, at a certain point in time with the development of combat, that when going into action all the rules of deployment and going into action should be observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let be a little bit more specific. First of all, in working with General Gotovina, do you know whether he was aware of the ballistic characteristics of use of artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was aware of the relative inaccuracy of artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did he ever express to you any concerns about the use of that kind of weaponry in a civilian-populated area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: He expressed it in the way that he asked for maximum precision and that a proportionality be respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what did you understand maximum precision to mean?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: As an artillery man myself, or an officer in the artillery, I understand that one sentence as meaning and implying all the actions that must necessarily be undertaken, in order to ensure that an artillery shell or rocket reach its target as precisely as possible. To hit the target as precisely as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: As an artillery officer, I take it you're aware that there is a range of error for every artillery weapon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, both objective and subjective.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And was General Gotovina, to your knowledge, aware that there was a range of error inherent in artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. And that is why he asked it to be reduced to the least possible measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what were the ranges of error of the weapons used to fire on Knin, or targets in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That depended on the distance from which the target was being targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let me be a little more specific then. The weaponry which you, in fact, used against targets in Knin, can you tell us, first of all, what that weaponry was, and what the ranges of error for each one of those weapons were, given where they were located.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The targets in Knin on the first day of the attack were targeted by a 130-millimetre cannon and the multi-barrel rocker launchers of 122-millimetre, BM 21. And on the second day during the attack, in the operation itself, there were a number of projectiles that were fired from Howitzers. The 122-millimetre D30-type Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let's focus first on the 4th of August. First of all, were there any other kinds of weapons used to fire on targets in Knin on 4 August, other than the 130-millimetre gun which you mentioned and the 122-millimetre multiple-barrel rocket launcher system.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the ranges of error were for each one of the guns that fired into Knin on that date. I'm sorry, I should also add rockets.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: For the 130-millimetre cannon, I can say that at a distance of 26 kilometres, I would -- or for that distance, I would have to consult the -- the firing tables because it is difficult to keep all that on one's mind. This is a range of probably error of about 14 or 15 metres for -- along the axis, but -- and as for distance, the errors is about 70 to 75 metres. But -- but to give you precise data, I would have to consult the firing tables, because these values change. As for MLRs, without consulting firing tables, I cannot say what the probable deviation would be, if they -- if they fire at targets that are at the -- at their -- the end of their range.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let me first start with the 130-millimetre guns. You indicated for the 130-millimetre cannon a range of 26 kilometres. There were two positions from which 130-millimetre guns were being fired on Knin; right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: There was TS-3 commanded by Mr. Mamic, which was in Operational Group North, correct, or in the area of Operational Group North, I should say; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And then there was TS-4 of OG Sibenik commanded by Mr. Milin; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: What was the distance from where the 130-millimetre guns and TS-3 were situated and their targets in Knin, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The distance topographically measured and at the end of their range was 27 kilometres. I'm referring to TS-3 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how about for TS-4, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I would like to provide explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Not -- this doesn't apply to all the targets in Knin but only to the extreme target. For TS-4 the first or closest target was about 25 kilometres away from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when you're giving these distances to targets, are you talking about targets within the town of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: In the settlement of Knin from the bridge to the north-east exit from the settlement toward the Dinara mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the 122-millimetre BM 21 multiple-barrel rocket launcher systems, can you tell us the distance between those weapon systems and the targets in Knin which they fired on, on 4 August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The closer target, the one closer to the positions of the BM 21 launchers in the north-east, in the direction of Mount Dinara, was 18 kilometres away and the farthest target about 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I understand you may not know the probable ranges of error of those weapons at that distance at this time. However, was the probable range of error of those weapons discussed with General Gotovina by you or anyone else, to your knowledge, prior to the decision to actually fire?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did he express any concerns to you regarding the probable ranges of error of those weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you can recall, what exactly were his concerns?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: He was concerned about the likely deviation of a missile or a shell to exceed the size of the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Were there any targets in particular that raised this concern, in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: For strategic level targets, there was such concern. I'm referring to the Main Staff of the so-called Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina and the system of the communications centre for the -- for the area of the so-called Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And for those two targets, were either of these weapon systems, the 130-millimetre cannon or the 122-millimetre multiple-barrel rocket launcher system, were they capable of being fired at these targets and hitting only those targets and nothing else around them. Was that a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: If we consider the whereabouts of the two targets, the location -- or, rather, with respect to the location of the targets it was only possible to target the railroad station. If we're speaking about the BM 21 MLR.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I want to make certain that I understand your answer, Mr. Rajcic. Are you indicating that the railway -- the railroad station is the only target in Knin which you could fire at with these weapons and not have the projectiles go beyond the limits of the target?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that, sir. I said around the targets that were the Main Staff of the army of the so-called Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You indicated that General Gotovina had expressed a concern about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I still do not fully grab the answer of the witness. Could you perhaps further explore what he exactly means.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm attempting to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You indicated that General Gotovina expressed a concern about the range of error, that the weapons might go beyond the actual targets. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I asked you to identify which targets in particular he had that concern about, about the projectiles landing beyond the target, and you indicated the Main Staff of the RSK and the communications centre of the RSK. And then when I asked about that, you added the railroad station. So I just want to be clear: What targets did General Gotovina indicate to you were a concern that shells would fall outside of the target?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Before I answer your last question, I must add a comment. You asked me whether there were other targets in the area that it was possible to shell with launchers and cannon, and then I said that the railroad station was such a target. And now coming to your last question. General Gotovina expressed concern about a possible or probable deviations of the projectiles outside the extent of the targets, and with regard to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina and the communications centre, which was in immediate proximity.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And with respect to those two targets, the Main Staff of the RSK, and the communications centre, were the 130-millimetre guns and 122-millimetre rocket systems, were they capable being fired at those targets and only hitting those targets and nothing else around them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you inform General Gotovina of that fact?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. That information was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you certain that he understood what you were telling him about that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: It isn't for me to judge whether the commander has understood. I apologise, but -- I apologise for replying to your question with another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Fair enough. Did he indicate to you why he nevertheless decided to go ahead and fire at those targets, knowing that the shells -- some shells which were fired at them would not hit those targets but would, in fact, hit the area around them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what he said?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: That there was the risk of some projectiles missing the targets, that the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina was a highly interesting target, or the target, par excellence, in combat. And that we should analyse the possible collateral damage, due to that handicap.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you analyse the possible collateral damage to be caused by firing artillery at targets in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what was the result of your analysis of possible collateral damage?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The analysis showed that it is possible that citizens come to harm to a lesser extent at Knin and that lesser material damage to the surrounding buildings is also possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When you say "harm to a lesser extent," lesser than -- lesser as compared to what?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Well, a lesser extent if we take into consideration the effect of contact-fuse shells. Those shells have the characteristics that they cannot pierce concrete buildings, and the projectiles cannot enter the inside of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to come back to that point a bit later, but I want to stick for now with the analysis of possible collateral damage. You compared -- or what did you compare the use of artillery to, in deciding what the relative amount of collateral damage would be?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The input for that analysis was, firstly, the tactical and technical characteristics of the target itself, the area of the target, the surface area, the surrounding buildings, the quality of construction; and we made your analysis, based on intelligence information, saying that at Knin, at the time when the shelling was to be effected, a curfew was in place. And as early as June, according to our intelligence, there had been substantial emigration of citizens from Knin, and at the given time, that is 5.00 a.m., the presence of civilians on the streets and in buildings, too, will be at the level of the -- the orders of the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina and their plans to provide for the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Rajcic: 130-millimetre guns are more accurate than multiple-barrel rocket launcher systems. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell me in what circumstances a 130-millimetre gun would be more accurate than a rocket system?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: The purpose of both types of artillery pieces is different. The 130-millimetre cannon can be used for targeting point targets; whereas, the BM 21 launcher, 122-millimetre calibre, can cover a certain area, taking into consideration all procedures and actions necessary for the concentration of projectiles upon their contact with the target be reduced to the least possible extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now when you say that 130-millimetre cannon can be used for targeting point targets, can you tell me how you define a point target, in terms of size?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: A point target can be defined as follows: A place, the coordinates of which; that is, X, Y, and Z are precisely defined. Which certainly implies a precise implementation of all operational procedures for the artillery piece to be positioned in the most accurate manner. Then a point target can also be an area which for the 130-millimetre cannon can be the size of the normal scattering of -- of shrapnel on the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand your explanation. I'm wondering if can you give us an area size; for example, 50 metres squared, or 25 metres squared. What you consider to be a point target that artillery system like a 130-millimetre gun is effective at firing at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: I can give you a rough explanation. 50 metres by 50, but that requires additional explanation. The normal scattering or dispersion of a 130-millimetre shell is an area with a diameter of 35 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how does that compare with a 122-millimetre rocket system, in terms of being able to effectively hit an area that size?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: It can be compared in different ways. Let me explain. The technical capabilities of the BM 21 MLR enable it to fire individual missiles, which means that you needn't always fire the entire set of missiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And that's what I'm attempting to determine. If you fire just one 122-millimetre rocket, is that going to be more accurate or less accurate than if you fired one 130-millimetre cannon?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: It can be just as accurate because the procedures and actions of preparation for firing are the same as in the 130-millimetre gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, a 130-millimetre cannon is essentially a very big gun. It fires one large shell under a charge; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is relatively large. It weighs 34 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And a rocket system is a projectile which leaves the system and arrives at the target under its own propulsion system; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: Yes. It has a -- it has rocket propulsion, rocket fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I'm looking at the clock. I have a matter to deal with for two minutes. I don't know whether you are exploring in full depth the two systems. That certainly would take quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I've got one or two more questions on this area, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would please put them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, does a rocket which is self-propelling propulsion system versus a shell, which has been fired out of a charge, do they have the same ballistic characteristics in terms of moving with the wind, in terms of -- can you tell me whether or not they are subject to the same ballistic characteristics and whether those characteristics affect the projectiles in the same way?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC
utterances.text: There can be ballistic difference, with regard to the active part of the trajectory while the rocket fuel is burning in the propulsion system. Whereas in the second part of the trajectory, both projectiles behave in the same way, given the same ballistic conditions. That is, in the stage when the shell or the rocket are flying freely toward the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm finished with this topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Russo. Mr. Rajcic, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00, but I would first like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone, anyone, whoever it is, about your testimony, the testimony already given, or testimony still to be given. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, although we will be in another courtroom, courtroom 1. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Rajcic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to deliver the decision of the Chamber on the motion to hear the testimony of Witness 13 via video-conference link. On the 11th of February, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting to hear the testimony of Witness 13 via video-conference link on the 24th of February, 2009. On the 13th of February, all three Defence teams informed the Chamber that they did not object to the Prosecution's request. On the same day, the Chamber decided to grant the request for a video-conference link and informed the parties accordingly through an informal communication. According to Rule 81 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Chamber may order that proceedings be conducted by way of a video-conference link if it is consistent with the interests of justice. As the Chamber has set out in numerous decisions in this case, the test of Rule 81 bis is met if a witness is unable to come to the Tribunal, if the testimony of this witness is sufficiently important to make it unfair to the requesting party to proceed without it, and if the accused is not prejudiced in the exercise of his or her rights to confront the witness. Medical documentation, attached to the Prosecution's motion, describes that Witness 13 suffers from angina pectoris, and indicates that the witness, because of her condition, cannot travel. On the basis of this, the Chamber is satisfied that Witness 13 is unable to travel to Tribunal to testify. Witness 13 is expected to testify about scheduled killing incident number 1 in the indictment. The Chamber is, therefore, satisfied that her prospective testimony is sufficiently important to make it unfair to the Prosecution to proceed without it. Finally, the Defence has not argued, and the Chamber does not find that the accused would be prejudiced in the exercise of their right to confront the witness. Consequently, the Chamber finds that it is consistent with the interests of justice to grant the Prosecution's request to hear Witness 13's testimony via video-conference link, and the Prosecution motion is, therefore, granted. This concludes the Chamber's decision on the matter. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 19th of February, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
